commits.message:
Feature/gh aw (#750)

* Add coverage-autofix workflow and gitattributes

Add a new repository automation spec (.github/workflows/coverage_autofix_every_3_days.md) that schedules a coverage health check every 3 days (and via workflow_dispatch). The workflow describes end-to-end coverage checks for Python and C++ (native and Dockerized across several distro images), failure handling, targeted minimal fixes, and PR creation rules using branch automation/coverage-autofix-every-3-days with labels and reporting requirements. Also update .gitattributes to mark .github/workflows/*.lock.yml as linguist-generated and use merge=ours for those files.

* Add generated workflow lock and docs; remove source YAML

Replace the original update_docker_python_versions workflow with its compiled artifacts. This commit adds .github/workflows/update_docker_python_versions.lock.yml (auto-generated by gh-aw v0.62.5) and .github/workflows/update_docker_python_versions.md, and removes the original .github/workflows/update_docker_python_versions.yml. The lock file is the compiled, immutable workflow; edit the .md source and run gh aw compile to regenerate.

* Simplify workflow schedule to weekly Saturday

Consolidate the Update Docker Python Versions workflow schedule and docs: replace the two exact-cron entries with a single cron and add a friendly comment in the workflow lock; update the markdown to describe weekly Saturday fuzzy scheduling and remove the previous America/Los_Angeles local-time guard. Also updated gh-aw metadata hash in the lock file.

@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+---
+name: Update Docker Python Versions
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  schedule: weekly on saturday
+permissions:
+  actions: read
+  contents: read
+safe-outputs:
+  create-pull-request:
+    title-prefix: "[docker-python-update] "
+    labels: [dependencies, docker, automated-pr]
+    draft: false
+    preserve-branch-name: true
+    if-no-changes: "ignore"
+engine:
+  id: copilot
+  model: auto
+network:
+  allowed: [defaults, python]
+tools:
+  edit:
+  bash: true
+---
+
+# Update Docker Python Patch Versions
+
+Update Docker Python patch versions by running the repository updater script, then
+open a PR if and only if docker-related files changed.
+
+## Schedule Behavior
+
+- If triggered by `workflow_dispatch`, run immediately.
+- If triggered by `schedule`, run once per Saturday using gh-aw fuzzy
+  scheduling.
+
+## Steps
+
+1. Run the updater script:
+   - `python .github/scripts/update_docker_python_versions.py --write`
+
+2. Check whether there are docker file changes:
+   - `git diff --quiet -- docker`
+
+3. If there are no docker changes, stop with a no-op summary.
+
+4. If docker changes exist, create or update one PR using:
+   - Branch: `automation/update-docker-python-versions`
+   - Base: `main`
+   - Title: `Update Docker Python patch versions`
+   - Commit message: `chore(docker): update Python patch versions in Dockerfiles`
+
+## Pull Request Body
+
+Include this summary in the PR body:
+
+- This PR updates the Python patch versions used by Docker images.
+- Updated files may include:
+  - `docker/**/Dockerfile`
+  - `docker/cache/download_build_cache.sh`
+  - `docker/**/README.rst`
+- Mention that it was generated by this workflow.
+
+## Scope
+
+- Keep changes restricted to docker Python version updates from the updater
+  script.
+- Do not make unrelated refactors or formatting-only edits.
